details: This package is a trojanized clone of the Baileys WhatsApp-Web library that hijacks the operator's WhatsApp account into following the publisher's channels and acting on their behalf. The injected code lives in lib/Socket/newsletter.js inside makeNewsletterSocket(), so it runs whenever a socket is created. It issues five hardcoded newsletter FOLLOW mutations (Types.QueryIds.FOLLOW over the w:mex newsletter query to s[.]whatsapp[.]net): four channel JIDs are hidden as base64 literals so they never appear as readable strings — MTIwMzYzNDAwNzA2MDEwODI4QG5ld3NsZXR0ZXI= (120363400706010828@newsletter), MTIwMzYzNDIzMjU3NTQ0NjQyQG5ld3NsZXR0ZXI= (120363423257544642@newsletter), MTIwMzYzMzQ5NDU3MTc2NDMwQG5ld3NsZXR0ZXI= (120363349457176430@newsletter), MTIwMzYzNDIxMDUyMDI3MTg4QG5ld3NsZXR0ZXI= (120363421052027188@newsletter) — plus the plaintext 120363408629601473@newsletter. Each of the four encoded JIDs is followed from a 90000 ms timer followed by a nested 5000 ms follow-up, and the plaintext channel is followed from a 30000 ms timer; the delays and encoding keep the subscriptions out of a quick read of the source and out of short-lived execution windows. The same module registers a messages.upsert listener that automatically posts a thumbs-up reaction to every incoming message from 120363408629601473@newsletter, impersonating user activity. lib/Utils/messages.js additionally stamps outgoing media with forwardedNewsletterMessageInfo pointing at 120363400706010828@newsletter ("Dew Coders OFC"). No credential, token, environment-variable, SSH or wallet file access and no destination outside WhatsApp's own endpoints were found in the package; the preinstall hook engine-requirements.js only compares the Node major version and exits. The package declares no repository and points its homepage and bugs URL at the WhatsApp channel 0029VbCbYpSEquiIsz0brA3D.
